Prepositions in legal English are essential for

. A single preposition can change the meaning of a clause, which is why legal professionals must use them carefully. Prepositional phrases often indicate obligations, rights, or conditions in legal documents.
The parties agree to the terms outlined in this contract.
The committee agreed on a new policy.
The company is liable for damages caused by negligence.
Subject to a penalty or action
The tenant is liable to eviction if rent is unpaid.
Non-profit organizations are exempt from taxation.
This contract is subject to approval by the board.
A trust is different from a will.
"The decision was made in accordance with company policy."
"With respect to the previous clause, additional fees may apply."
"The attorney signed the document on behalf of the client."
"The tenant must vacate the premises pursuant to Section 10 of the lease."
